picked.body: 기사 이해를 돕기위해 AI를 활용해 제작한 이미지입니다. 베트남 정부가 올해 처음 시행되는 '베트남 문화의 날'(11월 24일)을 당일 하루 휴무로 확정했다. 당초 근무일 하루를 주말과 맞바꿔 나흘 연휴로 조성하려던 계획을 철회한 것이다. 베트남 정부사무국은 이 같은 연휴 계획을 2일 발표했다. 이에 따라 공무원과 공무직근로자, 국가행정기관·공공서비스기관 근로자, 민간기업 근로자는 11월 24일 하루를 유급으로 쉬게 된다. 앞서 내무부는 11월 24일 당일에만 쉬는 안과, 근무일을 조정해 공무원·공직자가 나흘 연속 쉬도록 하는 안 등 두 가지 계획안을 두고 각계 의견 수렴에 나선 바 있다. 당시 정부 부처들은 대체로 연휴안에 찬성의 뜻을 나타내며 나흘 연휴가 조성되는 듯 했으나, 막판 재검토와 의견 수렴을 통해 당일 하루만 쉬는 수정안이 다시 제출됐다. 내무부는 수정안이 각 기관·단체의 근무일 조정을 유발하지 않으면서도, 유급휴가 권리와 문화의 날의 목적·의미는 그대로 보장한다는 입장이다. 나흘 연휴 무산의 배경에는 연휴가 11월 말에 위치한 것도 중요한 요소로 작용했다. 연말을 앞둔 가운데 각 기관·단체가 연간 업무계획을 마무리하는 시기이고, 많은 기업이 생산·납품 일정을 서두르며 경영계획을 마무리하고 다음 해를 준비하는 시기라는 점에서다. 결국 당일 휴무 방안이 채택되면서 공무원·공직자는 월요일인 11월 23일에는 평소대로 근무하게 된다. 베트남 문화의 날은 지난 1946년 호치민 초대주석이 주재한 제1차 전국문화회의을 기념해 정치국이 지정한 공휴일로, 국민들이 문화 활동에 참여하고 이를 누릴 수 있도록 하며, 문화예술인의 창작 활동을 독려하고 문화적이고 문명화된 생활양식을 확산하는 것을 목표로 한다. 정치국 결의안에 따라 베트남 국회는 지난 4월 매년 11월 24일을 베트남 문화의 날로 정하고, 이날을 공휴일로 지정하기로 했다. 따라서 올해는 베트남 문화의 날이 첫 시행되는 해다. 정부 역시 노동법에 베트남 문화의 날을 공휴일로 추가해 연간 공휴일 수를 기존 11일에서 12일로 늘리는 법안을 발의한 바 있다. 해당 법안은 이달 중 국회에서 심의·통과될 예정이다. 베트남 문화의 날이 공휴일로 지정됨에 따라 베트남의 연간 공휴일은 12일로 늘어났다. 여기에는 △신정 1일 △뗏(Tet 설) 5일 △훙왕기일(음력 3월 10일) 1일 △통일절(남부해방기념일, 4월 30일) 1일 △노동절(5월 1일) 1일 △국경절(9월 2일) 2일 △베트남 문화의 날 1일 등이 포함된다.

picked.t: [베트남 주간 이슈] 12년 걸린 고속도로 개통에 증시 대통합까지…베트남에 '판'이 깔린다
picked.body: 호치민시의 3분기 경제성장률(GRDP)이 10년 만에 최고치인 10%에 육박하고, 착공 12년 만에 남부 물류의 핵심인 고속도로 전 구간이 뚫렸다. 베트남 시장의 판도가 근본적으로 바뀌고 있다. 단순히 저임금 노동력을 노리던 시대는 끝났다. 삼성전기는 AI 기판, LS에코에너지는 방산용 희토류, 두산에너빌리티는 대형 에너지 인프라를 쓸어 담으며 베트남을 첨단 기술의 핵심 거점으로 탈바꿈시키고 있다.  여기에 299개 종목의 증시 일괄 이전과 엄격해진 규제 환경까지 맞물리며 '진짜 실력'을 겨루는 판이 깔렸다.  베트남 주간 경제·산업 동향 포인트 3가지 1. 대규모 인프라 및 친환경 에너지벨트 구축 가속화 롱탄신공항 개항 준비와 벤륵-롱탄 고속도로 전 구간 개통 등 대형 교통망 확충이 본궤도에 올랐다. 또한 2029년부터 전기차 배터리 재활용 의무화가 추진되는 등 친환경 기준이 엄격해진다. 2. 한국 대기업들의 첨단·에너지·소재 분야 대규모 투자 러시 삼성전기의 AI 기판 증설, LS에코에너지의 희토류 생산거점 구축, 두산에너빌리티의 화력발전 및 가스복합 수주 등 전통 제조업을 넘어선 첨단 기술과 에너지 협력이 두드러진다.  3. 디지털 경제·이커머스 중심의 내수 시장 고도화 이커머스와 SNS 쇼핑이 명절 성수기 매출을 견인하고 생성형 AI 사용률이 급증하는 등 베트남 소비 시장의 디지털 전환이 빠르게 진행되고 있다. ■ 행정부·정치·정책 '규제 고도화와 친환경 기준 강화' 베트남과 캐나다가 양국 관계를 ‘전략적 동반자 관계’로 격상하며 경제 및 외교적 협력 범위를 대폭 확대했다. 외국인 및 기관이 현지 근로자 구인 시 ‘국가고용플랫폼’에 채용공고를 게시하는 것이 의무화되어 고용 투명성이 높아진다. 2029년부터 판매량 기준 최소 8% 이상의 전기차 배터리 재활용이 의무화되며 친환경 규제가 구체화되고 있다. ■ 매크로·산업·경제 '수출 회복세와 디지털 소비 확산' 9월 제조업 PMI는 51.9로 전월 대비 1.4포인트 하락하며 경기 회복세가 다소 주춤한 모습을 보였다. 새우 수출이 8월 기준 33억 달러로 전년 동기 대비 12% 증가하는 등 농수산물 수출이 호조를 기록했다. 이커머스 쇼피와 틱톡숍의 월병 합산 매출이 1,600억 동에 육박하며 온라인 유통의 영향력이 급증했다. ■ 기업·금융·부동산 '전통 대기업의 신사업 진출과 증시 통합' 빈그룹이 1조 동 규모의 석유·가스 법인을 신설하며 신사업 진출에 박차를 가하고 있다. 하노이증권거래소의 모든 종목이 12월 말 호치민증권거래소로 이전 상장되며 자본시장 효율성이 강화된다. 미래에셋파이낸스 베트남이 중앙은행으로부터 예금 및 결제계좌 신규 사업 승인을 받아 핀테크 영토를 확장했다. ■ 인프라·하노이·호치민시 '교통망 완공과 메가시티 성장' 착공 12년 만에 ‘벤륵-롱탄 고속도로’ 전 구간이 개통되며 남부 경제권의 물류 효율성이 대폭 향상됐다. 호치민시의 3분기 GRDP 성장률이 10%에 육박하며 10년 만에 최고치를 기록했다. 하노이와 호치민시가 ‘디지털노마드’를 위한 세계 최고의 도시 상위 10위권에 진입했다. ■ 사회·한-베 이슈 '첨단 협력 확대와 다각적 진출' LS에코에너지가 베트남에 '방산용 희토류' 생산거점을 구축하며 핵심 광물 공급망 협력을 강화한다. HS효성이 다낭에 1억 달러 규모의 BCF 원사·카펫 생산공장을 착공하며 베트남 투자를 지속하고 있다. 두산에너빌리티가 8,380억 원 규모의 화력발전소 EPC 계약을 체결하는 등 에너지 인프라 수주를 이어갔다.

picked.t: Students rethink ‘American dream’ as costs rise and visa rules tighten
picked.body: At a study-abroad seminar held by Summit Education in Hanoi on Oct. 3, Nghiem Tan Cuong, a 10th-grade math major at Hanoi-Amsterdam High School for the Gifted, was looking into data analytics programs at universities in Singapore and Hong Kong. Cuong said the U.S. was once on his list, but his family changed course mainly because tuition there keeps rising, while his parents can afford about VND300-400 million ($11,500-15,400) a year. Tuition and fees for 2026-27 average $26,034 a year for out-of-state students at ranked public U.S. colleges and $46,973 at private ones, before living costs, according to U.S. News & World Report . He also sees Singapore and Hong Kong as modern places to study that are close to Vietnam, which saves on travel. Counseling desks for Asian universities stayed crowded throughout the event as students waited to ask about entry requirements, tuition and scholarships. Tran Minh Trang, a 10th grader at Phan Huy Chu-Dong Da High School, has also set aside plans for the U.S. and Europe to aim for business and economics programs at the University of Hong Kong (HKU) and the National University of Singapore (NUS). She described Asia as a friendly environment with good education where she can still use English. "The application process at Asian universities is also leaner and simpler than in the U.S., based mainly on GPA and certificates," Trang said. The shift from the U.S. to Asia is growing clearer, said Le Dieu Linh, deputy director of Summit Education, where most families used to target only American schools. In the past one to two years, 30-40% of its students have considered Asia and applied to schools in the region alongside the U.S., she said. HKU has seen a similar trend, with one Vietnamese applicant in 2022, three the next year and 30 in 2024, according to Vu Hai Truong, its admissions representative in Vietnam. This year the number rose tenfold to 300 applications, of which 192 were admitted, he said. Counselors and admissions officers point first to cost. Tuition and fees at ranked U.S. national universities have risen about 102% at private schools since 2007-08, 99% for in-state students at public schools and 89% for out-of-state students, or 18-26% after inflation, according to U.S. News & World Report data from 395 institutions. Their second reason is tighter U.S. rules on visas and work. Guidance issued in August by the U.S. Student and Exchange Visitor Program limits curricular practical training, a work authorization widely used for internships, to programs that require the training of every student. The H-1B work visa has moved from a random lottery to a selection weighted by four wage levels, with the highest-paid applicants entered four times and entry-level ones once. A $100,000 fee on new H-1B petitions for workers abroad, imposed in September 2025 and extended on Sept. 18 for another year, has made employers wary of hiring foreign graduates, the counselors said, though a federal court blocked its collection in June. Hong Kong is seen as "just Western enough," Truong said, offering parents and students the reassurance of a modern learning environment that is not too far from home. In the QS World University Rankings 2027, NUS ranks 10th, HKU 11th and Singapore's Nanyang Technological University 12th, followed by China's Peking University at 13th and Tsinghua University at 14th, with Fudan University at 26th. HKU charges non-local undergraduates HK$250,000-280,000 ($31,900-35,700) a year in tuition for most programs in 2027-28, according to its admissions office. Its 2025 bachelor's graduates earned an average of HK$33,338 ($4,250) a month, a university survey shows, and non-local graduates may stay in Hong Kong for two years after finishing without first securing a job. Another draw is "soft, simple entry requirements," said Nguyen Thuy Linh, an admissions representative of the Singapore Institute of Management. Where U.S. schools set high demands on essays, extracurricular activities, certificates and achievements, Singapore institutions mainly require a GPA of at least 7.0 out of 10 and an IELTS score of 6.0, she said, with essays mattering only for scholarship applicants. HKU has lowered its minimum GPA for Vietnamese applicants from 8.0 to 7.0, Truong said, as universities court students they rate highly for ability, studiousness and adaptability. It also runs a principal-nominated scholarship program with eight Vietnamese high schools, including Hanoi-Amsterdam, Chu Van An and Nguyen Sieu in Hanoi and Le Hong Phong and Tran Dai Nghia in Ho Chi Minh City, compared with four schools in Thailand and none in Laos or Cambodia. Le Dieu Linh advised students to research their field and career path carefully before applying instead of chasing rankings, while Nguyen Thuy Linh urged them to sharpen their spoken and written English so they can integrate confidently in an international environment.

picked.t: The hidden mental toll of chasing 'passive income' through affiliate marketing
picked.body: Boxes, a tripod and dozens of opened cosmetic products lie scattered across the floor as the 22-year-old checks her affiliate marketing dashboard. After a week of filming and posting videos, her estimated commission stands at just VND18,225 (US$0.70). Three months earlier, My had been scrolling through social media when she came across a stream of videos showing creators claiming to earn tens or even hundreds of millions of dong (VND10 million = $384.6) through affiliate commissions. Her VND8 million salary as an office worker suddenly became proof she was falling behind. Using her credit card, she paid over over VND5 million to buy lights, a microphone, and sample products. By day she works at a company, and by night locks herself in to edit videos until dawn. But with algorithms becoming stricter, videos with attached affiliate links like hers only garner a few dozen views each. "My daily commission isn't enough to pay the electricity bill for filming," she sighs. "After spending my own money on products and staying up all night, what I get in return is helplessness." Thu Huong, 28, an administrative worker in HCMC, is in a similar situation after joining "get rich" groups for moms. The thought of herself livestreaming while watching over her kids, and "making enough money to buy milk and diapers just by attaching affiliate links", caused her to spend over VND8 million on a mini vacuum cleaner, food containers, and smart household appliances for making review videos. She timed her livestreams to appear around noon and 9 pm, and there were sessions when she would talk for two hours until her throat became hoarse, but attracted few viewers and could not close a single order. After three months, her commissions totaled less than VND600,000, and product samples are piled up in every corner of her house. "Seeing other people flaunting their large number of orders, I blamed myself for being useless," she says. The stress has also been causing her to snap at her husband and children, making family life tense. My and Huong are two of hundreds of thousands of young people swept into the recent wave of affiliate marketing. Videos showing viewers how to "stay at home and earn passive income" and "make hundreds of millions a month with just a phone" flood social media. The fear of missing out makes many people believe this is an easy path to making money, one that anyone who joins can profit from. According to the affiliate marketing platform ACCESSTRADE Vietnam, the size of Vietnam's affiliate market increased dramatically in 2026, and is estimated to reach up to $1 billion this year, a 30-fold increase from 2022. This expansion is tied to the deep penetration of affiliate marketing into the revenue structures of e-commerce platforms. On average, revenues from affiliate programs account for up to 10% of major brands' total revenues, a remarkable jump from a modest 4% in 2022. Notably, on major e-commerce platforms like Shopee, an estimated 30% of total sales are generated directly from affiliate links of publishers and key opinion consumers. But the low barriers to entry have caused the market to quickly saturate. A large number of registered publishers end up going inactive, or earn less than VND1 million per month before quietly quitting, due to inventory losses and time pressure. E-commerce businesses also carry hidden cash flow risks such as order cancellation and return rates, slow reconciliation, and withholding tax obligations. A lack of understanding of cash flows and sunk costs causes many to join the market without knowing when they will break even. Vuong Nguyen Toan Thien, medical director at the Lumos Psychological Counseling and Therapy Center, says there are no precise statistics on the rate of depression or anxiety among people who do affiliate marketing, but the medical community has flagged what is known as "maladaptive social media addiction." International meta-analyses involving over 1.1 million young people show that uncontrolled social media scrolling is directly linked to sleep disorders, stress, and depression. "The harm does not lie in how many hours a day you glue your eyes to the screen," Thien says. "The real danger is when you lose self-control and let the habit of checking orders disrupt your sleep, fracture relationships, and drive yourself into psychological dead ends." According to experts, screenshots flaunting tens of millions in commissions on social media are powerful "bait" that trigger the fear of missing out. The internet often amplifies the success of a minority into a shared illusion, leading young people to mistakenly believe that anyone can easily transform their lives. They then throw themselves into the race while underestimating the price they might have to pay, forming a habit of constantly checking their screens and unable to disconnect. picked.t: Dollar up against dong on black market
picked.body: The greenback gained 0.27% to around VND26,030 at unofficial exchange points. The currency was firm at VND26,170 at lender Vietcombank. The State Bank of Vietnam increased its reference rate by 0.02% to VND25,643. Globally, the euro weakened sharply on Monday to a 17-month low as fiscal worries in France amid a steep bond market rout stoked fears of contagion risks in the region, helping the dollar shrug off soft US jobs ‌data that dented near-term rate hike expectations, Reuters reported. The euro slid to as low as $1.1161, its weakest level since May 2025 in Asian hours after clocking four straight weekly declines. Sterling slipped 0.24% to $1.32064, while the Japanese yen changed hands at 157.92 per dollar. That left the dollar index, which measures the US currency against six major units, up 0.47% at 102.37. "The dollar is the main winner in the current environment as not only is the rise in Treasury yields boosting the appeal of US ‌assets, but ⁠the broad selloff in debt globally is fuelling safe-haven flows into the greenback," said Matthew Ryan, head of market strategy at Ebury.

picked.t: Job interview no-shows spark debate over professional etiquette
picked.body: Dinh Minh Quyen, founder of a chain of English-language centers in Bien Hoa, Dong Nai, had scheduled an interview for 3 p.m. early last week. He had already spoken with the candidate by phone and provided details about the position, salary and bonuses, with both sides confirming the appointment. When the candidate had not arrived by 2:58 p.m., Quyen sent a message asking where they were. At 3:01 p.m., the candidate replied that they no longer felt the job was a good fit. Quyen said the candidate, who was under 25 and had relevant expertise, had handled the situation unprofessionally. To make time for the interview, he said he had asked his wife to travel 10 km to take their sick child to hospital. "It’s perfectly normal for a candidate to decide a job is not the right fit. But once an interview has been scheduled, giving advance notice if you need to cancel is simply a matter of respecting the other person’s time," he said. "If you can’t show the basic courtesy of giving advance notice when canceling an appointment, how will you compete in a few years in a job market full of smart technology and candidates who are both capable and considerate?" he asked. His social media post attracted thousands of reactions and quickly divided opinion. Some commenters agreed that failing to show up or cancel beforehand reflected poor communication and could damage a candidate’s professional image. They noted that the candidate had not contacted Quyen proactively and responded only after being asked about the missed appointment. Others argued that Quyen’s family arrangements were his own responsibility and should not be used to criticize the candidate. However, many commenters also pointed out that the candidate had not bothered to cancel himself and only responded only after the CEO sent a message. One comment said: "Not ‘ghosting’ (ignoring) people is basic courtesy. It should not become acceptable behavior simply because ‘all young people are like that these days,’" Many other employers also shared accounts of candidates failing to appear, blocking them or canceling interviews at the last minute. They viewed a candidate’s attitude toward an appointment as an early indication of how that person would work. A candidate’s silence until the last minute showed a lack of respect in communication, a commenter with the handle Hai Anh said. "Professional skills can be taught, but how someone handles an appointment is an early indication of how they work." The debate surrounding Quyen’s story touches on a longstanding issue in the labor market: candidates confirm interviews but then fail to appear or cancel at the last minute. Twenty-three percent of employers had been "ghosted" by candidates after confirming an interview time, a May 2026 survey by recruitment platform CareerLink found. No-shows occurred most frequently during mass recruitment drives, at a rate of 15–20%, Bui Doan Chung, founder of the Nghe Nhan Su Viet Nam (Vietnam Human Resources Profession) platform, said. Workers today have access to information about many jobs at once, and when another opportunity looks more attractive, they change their mind, he said. Ngoc Son, 24, an information technology employee in Hanoi, skipped scheduled interviews at two companies earlier this year. After receiving five interview appointments within a few days, Son attended only two and did not respond to the other companies. He said: "I didn’t know how to respond to them, so I didn’t answer their calls. I thought that if the company couldn’t hire one person, it would call someone else." Chung said a candidate’s absence should not automatically be used as evidence against their character. "In recruitment, a company is essentially selling a job opportunity." To avoid such situations, professional companies now focus on improving their recruitment processes. Automated reminders sent by email, digital calendar, SMS, or phone calls help them know in advance if candidates plan to cancel or reschedule. Many businesses also cancel interviews at the last minute or leave candidates waiting without explanation. CareerLink’s survey found that 58% of companies had, at some point, failed to respond to candidates after interviews. "Candidates have every right to turn down a job opportunity, but how they do so also reflects their professionalism. Respecting other people’s time is, first and foremost, a sign of self-respect," Chung said.

picked.t: Da Nang man arrested in $30,000 larceny from foreign tourist
picked.body: Da Nang police opened a criminal investigation against Tran Van Quan on Sept. 30 under the charge of "abuse of trust to appropriate property." According to investigators, Wang Qiang, 30, had successfully exchanged currencies through Quan several times before. On Sept. 13, Wang contacted Quan through WeChat to arrange another exchange of U.S. dollars into Chinese yuan. Quan went to Wang’s residence in An Hai Ward to collect the $30,000. He said he would find someone to exchange the money and transfer the equivalent amount to Wang’s bank account using the QR code Wang provided. After receiving the money, Quan blocked Wang on WeChat, removed him from his contacts and fled to Nha Trang. Wang reported the incident to police on Sept. 17. Da Nang criminal police tracked Quan down in Nha Trang and recovered the $30,000 from his backpack at the time of his arrest. Police said Quan subsequently admitted to taking the money. The investigation is continuing.
